By method: only removals of solid blocks start a search, on the page thread at `update()`; an unloaded chunk counts as holding; pieces are whole cubes for collider and mesh (slabs and stairs too), flat colour without the world's textures or light, and never go back into the world; non-solid blocks resting on a piece (flowers) stay where they were. | The search after an edit stops at a holding cell or `maxCells`, and a piece is built from whole cells in flat colour so it costs one body and one mesh per block type. | A loose group of `maxCells` blocks or more stays hanging, an overhang into an unloaded chunk stays up, and a falling slab looks like a full block without its texture. | Raise `maxCells` (up to 65,536) for larger pieces, load the neighbouring chunks before cutting, and pass `material` for your own look. |
| Voxel-edit shader brushes (`@margoengine/voxel-edit/shaders`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: 1 to 1,024 passes, up to 16 params, a 256-entry table of 0 to 255, values clamped to 255, a grid (and tool) within the device's storage binding limit (128 MiB by default) and `maxCells` (default 16,777,216). By method: every cell of a pass reads the grid as it was before that pass; one submit per pass; the whole grid is uploaded and read back per `run`; brushes see one grid and one tool grid. | Grids are packed four cells to a word in one storage binding, and the CPU builds the selection mask and counts changed cells. | A grid larger than the binding limit is refused, and each `run` pays an upload and a read-back. | Split a large model into tiles with `voxTiles` (`./vox`) and brush each. |
| Voxel-edit rigs (`@margoengine/voxel-edit/rig`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: unit quaternions (length within 0.001 of 1), unique bone names with parents listed first, parts on known bones, a baked box within `maxCells` (default 16,777,216). By method: each part follows one bone rigidly; a bake gives each cell the part cell under its centre, later parts over earlier ones. | Blocky characters move whole parts; blending cells between bones would tear the grid. | Turns other than quarter turns resample, so a turned part keeps its cell count only roughly; parts do not bend. | Use quarter turns for exact frames; for smooth skinning mesh the parts and use `@margoengine/rigging` with `@margoengine/animation`. |
| Voxel-edit GPU bulk edits (`@margoengine/voxel-edit/gpu`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: a grid within the device's storage binding limit (128 MiB by default) and `maxCells` (default 16,777,216, at most 67,108,864); fill radius 0 to 128; 0 to 1,024 iterations per filter; a 256-entry remap table of 0 to 255; a brush made on the grid's own device. By method: every edit reads the grid as the edit before left it; one submit per pass; a combine uploads its tool grid each time and counts clipped cells on the CPU. | Exact integer cell work keeps every result equal to the CPU operation. | A grid larger than one storage binding is refused, not split. | Split a large model with `voxTiles` (`./vox`) and edit each tile. |
| Voxel-edit shared editing (`@margoengine/voxel-edit/collab`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: a site name of 1 to 256 characters, 65,535 sites per replica, clock and seq 1 to 4,294,967,295, cells inside the grid, values 0 to 255, `maxCells` (default 16,777,216). By method: each cell keeps the write with the highest Lamport clock, the higher site name breaking a tie; an operation already applied is ignored. | Last writer wins per cell needs no server and no conflict step, and merges in any order. | Each cell keeps one value, so two users drawing over the same cells keep only the later stroke; a replica keeps 7 bytes a cell plus every operation seen (5 bytes per edited cell), with no compaction. | Start a new shared grid from a snapshot when the log grows too large; give each user a stable site name. |
| Goxel and VoxEdit files (`@margoengine/voxel-edit/formats`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: `.gox` versions 1 and 2 read, 2 written; BL16 blocks of exactly 64 x 64 pixels; at most 4,096 layers; `maxCells` (default 16,777,216) counts each layer's block bounds before cropping; names and dictionary values written up to 255 bytes. `.vxm` versions 3 to 13 read, 12 written; at most 255 materials (palette indices 1 to 255) and 255 models, all of one size; textures up to 2,048 and face lists up to 262,144 quads are skipped, larger ones refused. By method: from a clean-room specification, not from either program. | Neither format has a public specification; the one Margo reads was written from two programs' behaviour and eight sample files, and lists what it could not determine. | Skipped and lost on a round trip: `.gox` cameras, light, preview, material lists beyond one default on writing, layer matrices of plain layers (written as identity), and the fork-only PLAC, CLRH and CUST chunks; `.vxm` baked meshes, textures, surface data, palette chunks and the trailer. Unknown and so not checked: the `.gox` chunk CRC (no writer computes one; written as 0), the colour space of block colours, the meaning of alpha 1 to 254 (read as solid), clone layers under a rotating `mat` (each voxel centre goes to the cell it lands in), and the inside test at a shape's exact edge (centres on the edge count as inside); `.vxm` versions other than 4 and 12 (no sample files; version 13 in particular rests on one program's reader), the v6 to v10 texture compression, the pivot X convention of v10 and older (returned as stored), and whether VoxEdit opens a file with no baked mesh, as `writeVXM` writes. | Open a written `.vxm` in VoxEdit before relying on it; keep `.vox` (`./vox`) as the exchange file when a model must keep cameras, materials or meshes. |
| Voxel-net entities (`@margoengine/voxel-net/entities`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: `maxEntities` (default 4,096, at most 1,048,576), `maxPerPlayer` (default 256, nearest first), kind 0 to 65,535, state 0 to 255, `leaveRadius` at least `radius` (default 64 and 10% more). By method: entities over a chunk the server has not loaded do not move; each entity is quantized once per tick and sent as a delta against the player's last message; a player away (parked) gets every entity again in full. | Sending only what is near and changed keeps a crowded world within the 20 Hz tick and each link. | A world of many entities steps every one each tick on the server's thread, with no sleeping of far ones beyond unloaded chunks; brains run on the main thread; no pathfinding (only `wander`). | Keep entities near players; write your own brain for chase or flee; raise `maxPerPlayer` with care for the link. |
| Voxel-net shards (`@margoengine/voxel-net/shards`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: `regionSize` a multiple of 32 blocks (default 256), `margin` 0 to half the region (default 8), `secret` at least 16 characters, tickets good for `ticketLife` (default 10,000 ms) and once, a handed-off player closed with 4001 after `grace` (default 5,000 ms). Measured on loopback in one process only (two servers, real sockets); not measured between machines. | Each shard is a plain VoxelServer that owns its regions' edits; tickets carry the player across, so no shard needs another's state. | A shard sees only its own edits: the other side of a border shows as generated until the player crosses. A handoff keeps position, not velocity, and lands on the ground; the next shard sends the chunks around the player again. | Put busy areas inside one region; make regions larger than the view distance so borders are crossed rarely. |
| Voxel-net WebTransport (`@margoengine/voxel-net/webtransport`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: `inputCopies` 0 to 8 (default 3), the copies of one message at most 120 steps; a gap of more than 240 lost steps closes the client with 1002. Measured over an in-memory stand-in link only (a third of datagrams lost each way, every 5th survivor late): no step lost with 3 copies, client and server within 0.05 blocks. | Inputs are small, so copies cost little and make a lost datagram free; whole snapshots cost more bytes than deltas but need no acknowledgement. | A dropped session is not resumed. The slow-client check does not see a WebTransport stream backing up. Players snapshots go whole, so they are larger than over a WebSocket. | Connect again on close; keep `playerDistance` small for crowded worlds; use a WebSocket where WebTransport is missing. |
| Voxel-net chat and inventory (`@margoengine/voxel-net/chat`, 2026-11-09) | Enforced: client app messages at most 16,384 bytes and `appRate` 20 per second (burst 20) per player, the rest dropped; a chat line at most 256 UTF-8 bytes after cleaning, `rate` 1 per second (burst 5); inventories 1 to 1,024 slots (default 36), `stackLimit` default 64. Measured over real sockets on one machine only. | The server owns lines and items, so a client can only say a line or ask to move its own items. | Lines over the rate and moves that are not possible are dropped or answered with the slots as they are. Inventories live in server memory; no chat history for players who join later, no channels or mute lists. | Raise `appRate`, `rate` or `burst`; drop lines with `filter`; save inventories with `slots` and restore them with `load`. |
| Voxel-net lag compensation (`@margoengine/voxel-net/rewind`, 2026-11-09) | Enforced: `maxRewind` above 0 and at most 4,000 ticks (default 0.5 s); a view tick older is checked `maxRewind` back, a future one now; `maxDistance` default 64 blocks. Measured over real sockets on one machine only, a walker at 2.5 blocks per second. | A client draws others about `interpolationDelay` behind, so without rewinding its aim is behind the target. | A client can claim any view tick up to `maxRewind` back. Blocks are not rewound: one placed since the view tick stops the shot. Shapes blend in a line between ticks, as the client draws them. | Lower `maxRewind` to give a cheat less; pass `hitbox` for heads or capsules; call `shoot` yourself for shots of your own. |
| Voxel-net database store (`@margoengine/voxel-net/sql-store`, 2026-11-09) | Enforced: `table` letters, digits and `_`, at most 63 characters, optionally after one `schema.` (default `margo_chunks`); chunk coordinates -2^26 to 2^26-1. Tested on `node:sqlite` only; the Postgres SQL runs through SQLite, never against a Postgres server. | A folder with a file per chunk grows past what file systems list and back up well for large worlds. | On SQLite each query runs on the server's thread, so a slow disk stalls ticks. The store cannot list its chunks. | Use a Postgres `Pool` to keep queries off the thread; turn on SQLite WAL (`PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`); one `table` per world. |
| Voxel-net built-in TLS (`@margoengine/voxel-net/server` option `tls`, 2026-11-09) | Enforced: `tls` needs PEM `key` and `cert` that build a secure context, checked when the server is made and on `setTls`; a TLS handshake must finish within `helloTimeout` (default 3,000 ms). Tested over loopback with a self-signed certificate only. | Small hosts want `wss://` without running a reverse proxy. | `maxPending` and `maxPerAddress` count from the WebSocket upgrade on, so bare TLS handshakes are not capped by them. One certificate per server (no SNI choice between names); no HTTP/2. | A firewall or reverse proxy in front for floods, many names or HTTP/2; `setTls` for renewals; `tls: { ca }` on Node clients for a certificate of your own. |

## Rendering

| Limit | Starts at | Why | What you see | Escape hatch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One directional light in core | Enforced by design: core's lighting is one direction and one radiance, plus a colourless scalar ambient. | Every light model beyond one sun is an optional package, so apps that need one sun pay for one sun. | No API for a second sun in core; core's own ambient does not light metals. | `@margoengine/clustered`: up to 1,024 point and spot lights (`RangeError: Expected at most 1,024 lights` past that). `@margoengine/clustered/shadows`: shadows for up to 16 of them ([local-shadows-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/local-shadows-gpu.json)). `@margoengine/clustered/area` (8,946 B gzip): up to 64 rectangle area lights (`RangeError: Expected at most 64 area lights`), unshadowed, no texture bindings ([area-lights-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/area-lights-gpu.json)). More directional lights: `@margoengine/clustered/directional` (1,563 B gzip), up to 16 (`RangeError: Expected an array of at most 16 directional lights`), unshadowed. IES profiles: `@margoengine/clustered/ies` (3,697 B gzip), at most 16 distinct profiles, type C files only. Projector spots: `@margoengine/clustered/projector` (2,618 B gzip), at most 16 images of up to 4,096 texels a side. Physical units: `@margoengine/clustered/units` (833 B gzip). All three light entries use storage buffers, no texture bindings ([light-features-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/light-features-gpu.json)). Configurable ambient: `@margoengine/environment` `HemisphereLight` and `AmbientLight`, one per engine. Image-based lighting: `@margoengine/environment`. |
| 16 sampled textures and 16 samplers per shader stage | Enforced by WebGPU's guaranteed minimum; Margo's device asks for no more. gltf-pro's physical material with directional shadows, IBL and local shadows uses exactly 16 (asserted in [instancing.test.js](../packages/gltf-pro/tests/instancing.test.js)). | Every adapter, phones included, supports 16. Requiring more would make the same app fail on some devices. | A `RangeError` naming the combination, e.g. `gltf-pro: physical material + shadows + environment:lighting + clustered + clustered:shadows + shader patch needs 17 sampled textures per shader stage; this device allows 16`. | Drop one lighting feature for that material, or use the standard material (8 of 16 with everything attached). `VolumetricFog`, SSAO, clustered lights, area lights and light probes (`@margoengine/environment/probes`: one storage buffer; with an environment fallback they take EnvironmentLighting's place and its bindings) add no textures. Texture arrays are planned after 1.0. |
| float32 coordinates | Measured on the GPU ([large-coordinates-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/large-coordinates-gpu.json), 10 mm part, camera 50 mm away): core alone jitters 0.38 px at 1 km and 42 px at 100 km; at 6,000 km the part is not drawn. Per-stage CPU breakdown in [large-coordinates.md](large-coordinates.md). | Core and its kernel store positions and matrices in float32: half the memory and bandwidth of float64, and the format GPUs consume. | No error. Parts shake while the camera moves, small features collapse, specular shifts (2.8° at 100 km), and far enough out geometry disappears. | `FloatingOrigin` in `@margoengine/cameras/origin` (1,258 B gzip, 0 core bytes): 0.019 px jitter at every distance up to 6,000 km, and `engine.pick` hits the part at every distance ([large-coordinates.md](large-coordinates.md#the-plugin)). Vertices or child offsets that are already kilometres from their root inside one asset must be re-centred at export. |
| Transparency | Default: transparent materials and gltf-pro `BLEND` primitives are sorted back to front per mesh; core meshes are opaque. Measured ([oit-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/oit-gpu.json), a 50 % housing over gears orbited 360 × 1°): 13 steps with more than 1 % of covered pixels popping. | Sorting is exact for separate objects and needs no extra targets. | Popping where transparent parts interpenetrate or nest, as the camera moves. | `@margoengine/oit` (2,210 B gzip): 0 popping steps on the same orbit. Weighted blended OIT is an approximation: colour error against exact blending 0.5 / 4.6 / 8.7 (0-255) for 1 / 2 / 4 layers. Transmission and custom blending keep the sorted path unless `blending` is set; limits in its [README](../packages/oit/README.md#limits-the-wboit-approximation). |
| Screen-space reflections | Enforced by method: only what is on screen reflects. Core meshes and models passed to `ssr.add(model)` (gltf-pro, materials, terrain, water) show reflections; other custom shaders are reflected but do not reflect. Cost measured on a worst-case glossy floor ([ssr-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/ssr-gpu.json), quiet-gated): 2.2-2.3 ms at 1280×720, 5.8-5.9 ms at 1920×1080. | Reusing depth and colour that are already rendered avoids a second scene pass. Each custom pipeline needs its own capture into SSR's targets. | Reflections fade at screen edges and miss off-screen objects (reflection probes fill in where attached); water and terrain not added keep their own sky reflection. | `@margoengine/post/ssr` (9,068 B gzip) is itself the opt-in. Off-screen reflections: reflection probes in `@margoengine/environment/probes`; SSR removes the probes' own specular only where its ray hits on screen and keeps the probe's reflection elsewhere ([probes-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/probes-gpu.json): off screen the floor equals the frame without SSR, 95th percentile 0/255). Limits in the [post README](../packages/post/README.md). |
| Volumetric fog | Enforced by design: one froxel grid (default 160 × 90 × 64) whatever the screen size, so shadow edges in the fog are about one froxel wide (8 × 8 px at 1280 × 720). Effects measured in [volumetric-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/volumetric-gpu.json). | A froxel volume makes light shafts follow real shadows at a fixed cost per frame. | Particles, VFX, splats and transparent surfaces are fogged only when added with `fog.add` (additive, multiply and transmission surfaces never); nothing beyond `range`; local fog volumes only from `/fog-volumes`; no multiple scattering. Errors: `RangeError: Volumetric grid exceeds device limit`; `VolumetricFog replaces environment Fog '<name>': set its enabled = false or remove it`; `VolumetricFog needs scene depth: attach a post capture (Tonemap, Bloom, PostStack, SSAO, TAA) first or pass options.depth`. | `@margoengine/environment/volumetric` (6,923 B gzip) is itself the opt-in: a finer `grid` sharpens edges at a higher cost; `fog.texture` lets custom shaders (particles) sample the fog. Limits in the [environment README](../packages/environment/README.md). |
| Light probes (indirect light) | Enforced ([probes.ts](../packages/environment/src/probes.ts), [probes.test.js](../packages/environment/tests/probes.test.js)): one irradiance volume of at most 4,096 L1/L2 probes (64 per axis) and at most 16 box-projected reflection probes per `LightProbes`. The volume is baked; reflection probes are baked or captured live a few cube faces per frame (`setLive`; a moved box shows in a 128 px probe 7-11 frames later at one face per frame, capture GPU time per frame 0.066 ms or less and a median 0.20 ms on the prefilter frame, RTX A6000, [probes-live-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/probes-live-gpu.json)). Measured bake of 8 volume probes and one 128 px reflection probe 114-121 ms (diagnostic: other jobs running; [probes-gpu.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/probes-gpu.json)). Accuracy in the same file: volume SH within 1.7% of DC against an analytic room. | Baking turns the scene's light into lookups (no ray tracing per frame) and keeps them in one storage buffer, so no texture binding is spent. | Volume light stays as baked until `bake()` runs again; live reflection probes lag the scene by up to (probes + 1) refreshes of 6 / `facesPerFrame` frames and see only what the frame draws (render with `culling: false`); light leaks through walls thinner than the probe spacing (no visibility per probe); mirror-sharp reflections show texel-sized steps near wall edges at the default 128 px. Errors: `RangeError: Invalid irradiance volume: min < max, 1-64 probes per axis (4,096 in total), sh 1 or 2, blend >= 0`, `RangeError: Expected at most 16 reflection probes`, `RangeError: Light probe buffer exceeds device limit`, `light-probes replaces EnvironmentLighting: pass {environment} to LightProbes instead of attaching both`. | `@margoengine/environment/probes` (14,984 B gzip) is itself the opt-in: re-bake on demand or capture reflections live, one volume box per room against leaks, a finer `resolution` for sharper reflections. Dynamic GI: none yet. |
| Ambient diffuse under `KHR_materials_specular` | Enforced by method ([ibl.ts](../packages/environment/src/ibl.ts)): direct light and `Transmission` weight the base by one number, `1 - max(F)`, as the spec writes it. The split-sum ambient hooks (`EnvironmentLighting`, `LightProbes`, sky) keep what the specular term leaves per channel, so a coloured `specularColorFactor` tints their diffuse slightly. | The spec's scalar would change partly metallic texels of every plain material. | A faint complement tint on diffuse light from an environment, only with a coloured specular. | Light the surface directly, or use a grey specular colour. |
| Environment blend (`@margoengine/environment/blend`, 2026-11-07) | By method: a linear crossfade of two environments' radiance, `(1 - t) x from + t x to`, in the source cube, every prefiltered specular mip and the SH; on an Apple M6 (Metal) every texel of every mip equals the weighted sources within 3 x 2^-11 relative (rgba16float rounding of two inputs and the output; worst seen 9.5e-4) and a quarter-turned source lands texel for texel (LIM-493). Each source's `rotation` and `intensity` are baked in at each `update()`. | Prefiltering and SH projection are linear, so blending their results equals processing the blended image without prefiltering again on each change. | The output holds the memory of a third environment (its own source and specular cubes); the background shows the blended cube, not a source's sharper equirect; changing a source's rotation or intensity needs `update()`; not a time-of-day model. Cost not timed. | Use `@margoengine/sky` for a moving sun; call `update()` after changing a source. |
| Ground projected environment (`@margoengine/environment/ground`, 2026-11-08) | By method: per pixel the view ray meets the floor plane at `center`'s height or the dome (a sphere of `radius`), and the environment is read along the direction from the photo camera (`height` above `center`) to that point; on an Apple M6 (Metal) every pixel from two cameras equals a CPU mirror of that geometry within 0.15% and a floor point seen from the second camera keeps its colour within 0.13% (a plain background: over 3x) (LIM-498). `height` above 0 and below `radius`, `radius` finite, `center` three finite numbers. | Exact analytic geometry in the background's fragment shader; no extra pass. | The floor is flat and the dome a sphere, so walls and objects in the photo bend as the camera moves; the camera must stay inside the dome and above the floor; no contact shadow; cost not timed. | Pick `height` as the photo's tripod height; add `@margoengine/shadows` for contact shadows. |
| Dynamic global illumination (`DynamicGI` in `@margoengine/environment/gi`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: 1 to 64 probes per axis and at most 4,096, `probesPerFrame` 1 to 4,096, `resolution` a power of two 8 to 64. By method: one sweep of the volume every `ceil(probes / probesPerFrame)` frames, one more bounce per sweep; on an Apple M6 (Metal) a sunlit red wall's red bounce at a point in front of it falls from 0.51 to 0.09 (irradiance / PI) within one sweep after the sun moves behind the wall ((LIM-504)). | Re-capturing a few probes a frame spreads the cost of an irradiance volume bake over its sweep. | A change takes up to one sweep to show; light between probe centres is interpolated, so it leaks through walls thinner than the grid; no specular bounce; captures draw what the frame draws; cost not timed. | More `probesPerFrame` for faster response; a finer grid near thin walls; render with `culling: false`. |
| Probe visibility (`volume.visibility` in `@margoengine/environment/probes`, 2026-11-08) | By method: 24 direction bins per probe (cube face by quadrant) of mean and mean square distance, capped at 1.5 cell diagonals; Chebyshev visibility cubed and a smooth backface term per probe, renormalised. On an Apple M6 (Metal) the light leaking through a thin wall onto a dark floor falls from 0.092 to 0.00004 (irradiance / PI) and the on-screen pixel from 49 to 0 (LIM-543). | Coarse bins keep it to 192 B and one compute pass per captured face. | A bin averages a quarter face, so a wall that covers part of a bin only partly blocks it; a receiver whose eight probes are all occluded takes them equally; walls must be thicker than nothing at the probe's resolution; cost not timed. | Put probes on both sides of every wall; raise `resolution` for thin openings. |
| Sphere and blended reflection probes (`shape: 'sphere'`, `reflectionBlend: 'weighted'` in `@margoengine/environment/probes`, 2026-11-08) | By method: a sphere probe's parallax point is the far hit of the reflected ray with its sphere and its fade runs past the surface; weighted blending sums probes by fade weight, normalised past 1; on an Apple M6 (Metal) both match a CPU mirror within 3.2e-7 at 512 random rays (LIM-549). | No cost without them (box probes in order keep their shader text); a sphere adds one ray-sphere solve per probe per fragment. | Spheres are centred where they are created; capture still sees through each probe's own position only; cost not timed. | Use spheres for round or open areas and weighted blending where probes overlap at a doorway or a clearing. |
| Local fog volumes (`@margoengine/environment/fog-volumes`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: at most 256 volumes per `FogVolumes`, axis-aligned boxes (`min` < `max`) and spheres (`radius` > 0), `density` 0 to 1,000 per m, `noise` 0 to 1. By method: each froxel adds every volume's extinction and albedo-weighted scattering to the fog's; on an Apple M6 (Metal) the integrated volume of a box, a sphere and a noisy box equals a CPU mirror of the froxel pass within 0.002 + 1% (LIM-545). | The volumes share the fog's froxel grid, so they get its lighting, shafts, shadows and reprojection for one buffer read per froxel and volume. | Every froxel tests every volume, so the froxel pass grows with the count (cost not timed); a volume thinner than a froxel is blurred over it and its neighbours; boxes do not rotate; a volume cannot remove global fog. | Keep the count small and the volumes larger than a few froxels; raise `grid` for small volumes. |

| Materials surfaces outside the colour pass | Enforced ([cutout-passes-browser.mjs](../packages/materials/test/cutout-passes-browser.mjs), [cutout-casters-browser.mjs](../packages/shadows/test/cutout-casters-browser.mjs)): shadow maps, contact shadows, TAA velocity and picking follow `map` alpha, `alphaMap`, UV transforms, `alphaTest`, `vertexColors: false`, `displacementMap` and `clippingPlanes`. | Astronomical sky (`@margoengine/sky/astro`, 2026-11-07) | No counted threshold; the planet elements are valid 1800 to 2050. | Each part uses a published method with a stated accuracy. | By method: the sun by Meeus' low-accuracy method (about 0.01 degree), the moon by his chapter 47 series (about 10 arcseconds) with its parallax, the planets by Standish's Keplerian elements (valid 1800 to 2050; tens of arcseconds, several arcminutes for Saturn), nutation by the short series (0.5 arcsecond); aberration (up to 20.5 arcseconds) is not applied, Saturn's magnitude leaves out its rings, and the planets are points, not discs. Delta T is Espenak and Meeus' polynomials (to their fits, 0.6 s apart where they meet). Stars are points of a 1 px Gaussian with no twinkle; on a float target the sky behind a star is dimmed by 1/64 of the star's alpha (an 8-bit target replaces it by the alpha), and stars are drawn over the moon's disc. | Subgroup kernels (`@margoengine/compute/subgroups`, 2026-11-05) | Measured ([compute-subgroups.mjs](../examples/package-benchmarks/compute-subgroups.mjs), RTX A6000, subgroup size 32, 16,777,216 f32 values, busy machine, diagnostic, [result](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/compute-subgroups.json)): sort 11.9 to 7.0 ms (1.7 times), argsort 13.6 to 8.8 ms (1.5 times), sum 0.087 to 0.066 ms (1.3 times), sum along an axis 0.59 ms both, cumsum 0.55 to 0.56 ms (no gain). | Neural networks (`@margoengine/compute/nn`, 2026-11-05) | Enforced by method: f32 only. | Graph algorithms (`@margoengine/compute/graph`, 2026-11-05) | Enforced by method: vertices below 2^30; distances in `shortestPaths` are f32 sums, exact up to 2^24 for whole weights. `bfs` and `shortestPaths` take up to one round per edge of the longest shortest path (`shortestPaths` at most the vertex count, plus one to tell a negative cycle apart), and `connectedComponents` takes about log(vertices) rounds on the graphs tested (2,000-vertex shuffled path: under 64). Speed is not measured. | Each round runs over every edge at once with an atomic minimum, so a graph needs no frontier queue, the code is the same on the GPU and the CPU backend, and negative weights work. | A round visits every edge whether or not its source changed, so a long thin graph costs edges x its depth: a frontier-based search would do less work there. With f32 sums, cycles of total weight 0 that round below it can read as negative; zero-weight cycles can loop `predecessors`. `graph()` builds on the CPU and uses memory for every edge twice over. Not included: strongly connected components, minimum spanning trees, centrality. | Use whole or dyadic weights for exact sums; raise `checkEvery` on deep graphs to read back less often. |
| Workgroup autotuning (`@margoengine/compute/autotune`, 2026-11-05) | Default: 6 candidate sizes, 2 warm-up and 7 timed runs each, so 54 runs of your kernel on the first call and none on later ones. Results last for the context, or across sessions with `store`. | Measuring beats a fixed rule because the best size depends on the GPU and the kernel; timed runs take turns so drift is shared, and the median drops spikes. | The first call pays for those runs and for compiling every candidate. A result holds for the input size measured: name it in `signature`. Browsers round GPU timestamps (steps of 0.066 ms in the Chrome tested), so sizes of a short kernel can tie. Browsers without `device.adapterInfo` (and browsers that hide adapter details) let different GPUs of a store share an entry, which costs speed, never correctness. Driver updates are not seen: use `refresh`. `tuneCompute` covers the context's `reduce`, `scan` and `sort` only: `sum(axis)`, segmented scans and the element-wise kernels keep their fixed sizes, and the CPU backend, `useSubgroups` and the layer's sort ignore the table. The gain depends on the GPU: 8 to 13 percent on a sort on an Apple M6, none on the RTX A6000, where the default 256 is already the best. | Tune once at start-up, or ship a `store`. |

One draw would either cut the ramp or write depth through it. | Twice the vertex work for these lines; a translucent depth-writing line hides what is drawn behind it after it. | Leave `depthWrite` off where lines do not cross, or set `antialias: false` for one draw. |
| GPU picking of lines (`LinePicking` in `@margoengine/lines/pick`) | Enforced: 268,435,456 segments per pick, 8 overlays per `Picking`. By method: a pick answers the nearest thing only; `engine.pick` can only answer meshes, so a line that follows no mesh answers an empty stand-in mesh (`lineOf` maps it back); with an overlay registered every pick draws the 3 x 3 pass with all line vertices, uncropped. | Core is frozen, so `engine.pick` keeps its mesh return type; lines share the pass and depth test of meshes. | Picks cost more with many segments; Picking's cached ID texture goes unused. | Read `hit.line` from `picking.pick`; use `intersectLines` from `@margoengine/bvh/lines` for a sorted list of ray hits. |
| Trails (`Trail` in `@margoengine/lines/trail`) | Enforced: 2 to 65,536 points (`maxPoints`, default 256); past that the oldest point goes and the far end jumps. By method: a trail is a line, so it faces the camera unless `normal` lays it flat (2026-11-07), and a flat trail is one strip with a per-point `normal` it does not have: it lies in a plane facing that one direction, so it does not follow a hill, and its segments are not joined at a corner; a flat trail takes no dashes; a dashed trail ignores `tailWidth`, because dash distances use the value widths are stored in. | One line keeps joins, antialiasing, fog, clipping and picking for free. | A tyre track seen from low down looks like a tube, not a flat strip. | Raise `maxPoints`; build a flat strip as a mesh with `@margoengine/splines/mesh`. |
| Massive line batches (`LineBatch` in `@margoengine/lines/batch`) | Enforced: 67,108,864 segments a batch; one draw per 8,388,608 segments at the default 256 MiB `maxBufferSize`. By method: independent segments with square ends: no joins, round caps, dashes, fog, clipping planes, depth writing or picking; colours at 8 bits a channel; a CPU copy of 32 bytes a segment stays for device loss. | Six vertices and 32 bytes a segment, where `Line` draws 78 vertices and reads a storage buffer whose binding size limits it. | Translucent corners are darker where segments overlap; memory is 64 bytes a segment across CPU and GPU. | Use `Line` where those features matter. |
| Hidden lines (`HiddenLine` in `@margoengine/lines/hidden`, `behind` and `depthBias` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: the test is against scene depth, so surfaces that write no depth hide nothing; `depthBias` (default 0.001 of the distance) decides what counts as on a surface, so an edge closer behind a surface than that shows as seen. Dashes run in world units. Hidden lines do not pick. | A depth test is one draw with no mesh analysis, on any scene; exact CAD hidden-line removal would need the geometry on the CPU. | A very thin wall can show an edge behind it as seen. | Lower `depthBias`, or raise it if a far model flickers. |
| Alpha to coverage on lines (`alphaToCoverage` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: works with MSAA only and falls back to blending without it; opacity comes in steps of one sample, four at 4x MSAA; lines of equal opacity use the same samples, so the later replaces the earlier at a crossing. | MSAA hardware turns alpha into a sample mask, which is what makes it independent of draw order. | Fine opacity changes band at low sample counts. | Leave it off and blend, or raise the sample count. |
| Filled helpers (`solidHead` on `ArrowHelper`, `fillOpacity` on `PlaneHelper`) | By method: a fill is flat colour with no lighting and does not pick. An opaque fill writes depth; translucent fills blend in the order added. | Helpers are guides, so they stay readable in any light and need no material or mesh. | A solid head has no shading, so its shape reads from its outline. | Use a mesh from `@margoengine/core` where lighting matters. |
| Video output (`@margoengine/headless/video`, `/ffmpeg`, 2026-11-05) | `encodeVideo` builds the whole file in memory and needs WebCodecs: browsers and workers have it, Node does not. WebM takes VP8, VP9 and AV1; MP4 takes H.264, VP9 and AV1. WebM times are whole milliseconds, as its default timestamp scale gives. Alpha is dropped. Frames are 8-bit RGBA, so no HDR video. Sound is Opus in WebM and AAC or else Opus in MP4, one or two channels, and comes as plain samples held in memory. | A file built whole has every size known up front, so nothing is patched afterwards and the MP4 index can sit first for playback before the download ends. WebCodecs is the only encoder a page has; shipping one would be a large download. | A very long capture must fit in memory, as compressed bytes only. In Node, `encodeWithFFmpeg` streams to a file instead, and needs ffmpeg installed. The H.264 and VP9 arguments and the rawvideo input ran on real ffmpeg 9.0.2 (`npm run test:real-ffmpeg --workspace @margoengine/headless`): 12 frames each, BT.709 tags read back, colours within 2 of 255 levels. That run needs ffmpeg, so the unit tests keep a stand-in program for failures and aborts. | Render in a browser or worker for `encodeVideo`, or use `/ffmpeg` in Node. Pass `args` to choose other ffmpeg settings. |
| Subsurface scattering blur (`SSS` in `@margoengine/post/sss`, 2026-11-07) | By method: screen space, so only what is on screen scatters; one Gaussian per channel stands in for a measured profile's sum of Gaussians (no long red tail); the kernel stops at 64 px each side, so a surface filling the screen close to the camera scatters less than `radius` asks; taps across a depth step larger than `radius`, off the mask or on the background count as the centre colour. The mask is the user's: a material's `subsurface` value does not mark pixels by itself. One `rgba16float` texture at the frame size; GPU cost not measured (LIM-434). | A separable blur costs two passes of `2 x taps + 1` reads, where a 2-D kernel would cost its square. | Soft skin, wax and marble on marked pixels; red bleeds farthest into shadow edges with the default profile. | Raise `taps` for wide kernels; mark pixels with a `SceneTargets` output or a selection mask. |
| Material decals (`MaterialDecals` in `@margoengine/post/material-decals`, 2026-11-07) | By method: a screen-space relight in a PostStack, not a G-buffer write before lighting. The surface comes from a `SceneTargets` capture (one more scene pass); the change is core's lit model (sun plus ambient) for the new surface minus the old, so gltf-pro and materials models get the sun and ambient part only, not their image-based light; the sun's share is read back per pixel from the lit image, so a pixel the unshadowed sun gives nothing (facing away) is treated as lit; transparent effects drawn over the surface are relit with it; the atlas is read at mip 0; 64 decals, no culling; GPU cost not measured (LIM-441). | Engines that write decals into a deferred G-buffer change the surface before any light; Margo's forward renderer has no such buffer, so the relight works from a capture. | Normal, roughness, metalness and base-colour decals on any surface core or the capture draws, with shadow kept. | Keep decals on core meshes for an exact relight; give the atlas texels as wide as the decal's screen size. |
| Rough reflections (`SSR` with `stochastic: true` in `@margoengine/post/ssr`, 2026-11-08) | By method: one GGX-sampled ray per pixel per frame on surfaces rougher than half of `maxRoughness`, averaged over frames by a history reprojected with the surface's motion and clamped to this frame's 3x3 neighbourhood (mean plus or minus one standard deviation), blend floor 1/16; only what is on screen reflects, as for the mirror path. One history per SSR (a second view in the same frame reprojects against it); a moving camera smears rough reflections for a few frames; some noise stays on a still view (mean frame-to-frame change 0.15/255 against 1.28/255 at the second frame); three more `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-446). | One ray per pixel keeps the cost of the mirror path; the frames do the averaging. | Rough floors and brushed metal reflect what is on screen instead of keeping only the environment. | Leave `stochastic` off for deterministic frames (screenshots, tests); pair with TAA for a moving camera. |
| Multi-bounce screen GI (`SSGI` with `multiBounce: true` in `@margoengine/post/ssgi`, 2026-11-08) | By method: each frame adds one bounce by reading the light at ray hits from the previous frame's result, reprojected through the previous camera; only what is on screen bounces; the extra bounces trail a moving camera or light by a few frames; a hit hidden in the previous frame takes the light of what covered it for a frame; one history per SSGI (a second view in the same frame shares it); two more `rgba16float` targets and a display pass when SSGI ends the stack; GPU cost not measured (LIM-455). | Bounces accumulate over frames for the cost of one bounce per frame. | Indoor scenes fill with bounced light on a still or slow camera. | Keep it off for a fast-cutting camera, or accept a few frames of build-up after each cut. |
| Anamorphic streaks (`Anamorphic` in `@margoengine/post/anamorphic`, 2026-11-07) | By method: streaks are horizontal only (no rotation); they are built at half width and a quarter of the height, so a streak is about 4 px tall and a light smaller than a pixel still draws one; each streak is the light's own colour times `tint`, with no spectral split; reach is 2 (3^passes - 1) half-width texels each side; two quarter-size and one full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-459). | A chain of sparse 9-tap passes reaches far for a few reads per pixel, where one wide kernel would read hundreds. | Bright points and highlights draw thin tinted lines across the frame. | Lower `passes` for short streaks, raise `threshold` so only lights streak. |
| Blur (`Blur` in `@margoengine/post/blur`, 2026-11-08) | By method: 2 radius + 1 texture reads per pixel per pass, so cost grows with the radius (64 at most, 129 reads a pass); the kernel is cut at 3 sigma for the Gaussian; edges clamp to the nearest pixel, so a bright border bleeds inward; `region` is a rectangle with a hard edge; one or two full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-472). | A plain separable loop is exact for every radius and needs no mip chain. | Menus behind glass, focus pulls and custom chains blur by any whole-pixel radius. | Keep the radius small on weak GPUs, or chain two Blurs of half the radius for a wider, cheaper look. |
| Lens model (`Lens` in `@margoengine/post/lens`, 2026-11-08) | By method: one radial distortion term (k r^2), no tangential or chromatic part; distortion resamples the frame bilinearly, so it softens it slightly; the dirt is lit by its own glow at an eighth of the frame size (reach about 50 px), not by the glow of `Bloom`; the built-in dirt is a fixed pattern; two eighth-size and one full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-474). The Panini projection is a camera (`WideAngle` in `@margoengine/cameras/panini`), not part of this effect. | One term covers the usual barrel and pincushion look; a small glow keeps the dirt cheap. | Wide lenses bulge, and smudges on the glass light up around bright lights. | Pass your own `dirt` texture; set `dirtIntensity` 0 for distortion alone. |
| Billboards (`BillboardLayer` in `@margoengine/sprites/billboard`, 2026-11-08) | `capacity` 256 billboards before a buffer grows; at most the device's `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` / 64 per view. | One instanced draw per view, each view with its own sorted buffer, so its memory is 64 B per billboard per view. | By method: blended billboards sort by the pivot's distance, so two that cross draw one over the other whole; pixel-sized ones take their depth from the pivot; `lockY` applies to world sizes only; texels are read with no filtering. Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, by measured pixel extents. Time not measured. | `transparent: false` (cut-out with depth writes) needs no sort; split crossing quads into two billboards. |
| Smooth sprites (`SpriteLayer` `filter: 'linear'` in `@margoengine/sprites`, 2026-11-08) | One copy of the atlas per layer, `rgba8unorm-srgb` with a full mip chain: 4/3 of the atlas size again. | Filtering straight alpha bleeds a transparent texel's colour into edges, and filtering sRGB bytes darkens averages, so the layer keeps a premultiplied, linear-light copy. | By method: mip levels below the first average across neighbouring cells; the copy is made once, so a changed `GPUTexture` atlas needs `setAtlas` again; normals stay exact-pixel; premultiplied 8-bit storage loses colour precision at low alpha. Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, against the bilinear formula. Time not measured. | A gutter around cells drawn very small, or `mipmaps: false`. |
| Live grading (`Grade` in `@margoengine/tonemap/grade`, 2026-11-08) | By method: display-referred, on 0..1 colour after the tone curve; under an HDR `ColorOutput` what lies above white passes ungraded; curves are sampled 33 times and read linearly; the wheels are additive offsets with fixed luminance masks (no pivot or range controls); one uniform of 608 B; GPU cost not measured (LIM-477). | Grading after the curve keeps the controls in the 0..1 range artists know from grading tools. | Wheels, curves and hue against saturation move live with no LUT to bake. | Bake a LUT with `setLUT` for a look outside these controls. |
| Sprite shaders (`SpriteLayer` `shader` with `@margoengine/sprites/shader`, 2026-11-08) | One shader per layer; four `params` per sprite; outlines reach 1 to 4 texels; palettes 1 to 16 pairs. | A layer is one pipeline and one instanced draw, so the code is per layer and the per-sprite part is data. A shaded layer packs 64 B per sprite instead of 48. | By method: effects see one texel at a time plus `spriteTexel` neighbours inside the sprite's rectangle, so an outline needs transparent texels around the art; a palette swap matches exact bytes, so it is for `filter: 'nearest'`; WGSL that does not compile shows as a validation error on the first frame, not a throw. Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, against values worked out in the test. Time not measured. | Several layers for several effects; your own `spriteShader` for anything else. |
| Classic curves (`curve` `reinhard`, `cineon`, `linear` in `@margoengine/tonemap`, 2026-11-08) | By method: Reinhard is per channel (it shifts hue in saturated highlights) and never reaches white; Cineon is the filmic fit with its 2.2 gamma undone, not a film-stock model; linear clips at white; under an HDR `ColorOutput` they are scaled by the same rolloff as AgX and ACES; not compared side by side with another engine (LIM-479). | They exist to keep the look of scenes ported from engines that use them. | A ported scene keeps its contrast and highlight roll-off. | Use `neutral` or `agx` for new work. |
| Several atlases per layer (`SpriteLayer` with a list of atlases in `@margoengine/sprites`, 2026-11-08) | Up to the device's `maxTextureArrayLayers` (at least 256) atlases, all the same size. | A texture array holds same-size layers, which is what lets one draw read them all. | By method: the layer copies the atlases into its own array (one more copy of each in GPU memory), so a changed `GPUTexture` needs `setAtlas` again; a page sprite packs 64 B (80 B with a shader); `normals` need a single atlas. Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, byte for byte. Time not measured. | Pad smaller sheets to one size; a separate layer for normal-mapped sprites. |
| Custom tone curve (`CustomCurve` in `@margoengine/tonemap/custom`, 2026-11-08) | By method: a JavaScript curve is per channel, sampled at 128 points over 2^-12 to 2^8 (log2) and held above; a WGSL curve is compiled into the presentation shader, so a WGSL error shows as a GPU validation error; shader-node graphs are not taken directly; one uniform of 592 B; GPU cost not measured (LIM-481). | Tonemap does not depend on `@margoengine/shader`; sampling keeps a JavaScript curve live without a recompile. | Write a node curve as WGSL. | Use `wgsl` for exact or per-pixel curves. |
| Metering modes (`autoExposure` `metering`, `method` in `@margoengine/tonemap`, 2026-11-08) | By method: 4,096 samples on a 64 by 64 grid (a spot narrower than a few pixels resamples the same pixels); the histogram has 64 bins over -12 to 12 stops, so its level moves in 0.375-stop bin centres weighted by the kept share; centre weighting has a fixed sigma of a quarter of the view height; the mask is read by nearest texel; GPU cost not measured (LIM-482). | One workgroup keeps metering to one dispatch with no readback. | A finer histogram or more samples would cost more threads or passes. | Use `mean` for smooth adaptation, `histogram` for scenes with small lights. |
| 2D skeletal animation (`@margoengine/sprites/skeletal`, 2026-11-08) | Four bones per vertex; skinning on the CPU every frame for every visible mesh, about 20 B per vertex uploaded each frame. | Linear blend skinning is a weighted sum per vertex, cheap enough on the CPU for character meshes, and it keeps skinning testable in Node. | By method: linear blend skinning collapses a joint bent far (each vertex lies between its bones' rigid copies, so a sharp bend loses area), so give bends a shared, half-weighted vertex row; texels read exactly with no filtering, single-sample target; clips are linear keys only (no curves, events or blending between clips). Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, byte for byte. Time not measured. | More grid rows at joints; your own pose code that sets `Bone` fields before `skeleton.update()`. |
| Local exposure (`LocalExposure` in `@margoengine/tonemap/local`, 2026-11-08) | By method: the bilateral blur is separable (horizontal then vertical), an approximation of the 2D filter that can leave a faint halo along thin bright lines; quarter-resolution base (4 by 4 blocks); the whole source is filtered, not one view rect; three r32float textures (about 1.5 MB at 1920 by 1080); GPU time not measured (LIM-486). | Separable passes keep the cost linear in the radius. | Very fine structures are not separated into their own regions. | Lower `edges` for sharper region borders. |
| Sprite masks (`SpriteLayer` `mask` in `@margoengine/sprites`, 2026-11-08) | One rect or circle per layer, hard edged. | The test runs per pixel in the layer's fragment shader against one uniform, so a mask costs no extra pass or texture. | By method: a pixel is in or out by its centre, so edges step by whole pixels and do not antialias; a turned or scaled shape needs a rect or circle (no polygons or image masks). Every layer's uniform grew from 16 to 48 B for it. Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, pixel for pixel. Time not measured. | Draw into a `target` and composite it with your own mask pass for soft or image masks. |
| Isometric, staggered and hexagonal maps (`@margoengine/tilemap/iso`, `/hex`, 2026-11-08) | The cells in view are written each frame, 48 B each; one draw per run of one tileset in paint order. Oblique maps, and infinite maps that are not orthogonal, are refused by the Tiled importer; `fromTMX` (TMX through `@margoengine/loaders`) reads orthogonal maps only, as the loader does not carry the orientation. | Drawing in paint order across the whole view is what lets tall tiles cover the cells behind them; a cached 64 x 64 chunk per draw, as `TileMap` uses, would draw a tall tile on a chunk's edge under its neighbour's cells. | By method: the CPU cost grows with the cells in view (not measured); a turned hexagonal tile's edge pixels fall where rounding puts them; a tile wider than its cell may overlap a cell drawn later in the same row. Proved on one GPU, an RTX A6000, pixel for pixel against images painted from the layout rules. Time not measured. | Orthogonal maps draw with `TileMap` and its chunk cache; split a huge view into several targets. |
| Grid pathfinding (`@margoengine/tilemap/path`, 2026-11-08) | Up to `maxCells` (default 1,000,000) cells searched per call; arrays of the grid's size (about 21 B per cell) made per call. | A tile map is a grid, so a plain heap search over its cells needs no navigation mesh. | By method: one search per call on the calling thread (no incremental or hierarchical search, no jump point pruning); costs are per cell entered, not per edge; a staggered map's left and right cells in one row are two steps apart. Time not measured. | For big open worlds use `@margoengine/navmesh`; for many units to one goal reuse one `flowField`. |
| Field of view and fog of war (`@margoengine/tilemap/fov`, 2026-11-08) | One scan of up to `max(width, height)` rows per octant per viewer on the calling thread; a mask of `width * height` bytes per call (or the `into` mask), `FogOfWar` keeps two. | Shadowcasting visits only the cells that light can still reach, so a closed room costs its own cells. | By method: sight is from the viewer's cell centre and not symmetric; orthogonal and isometric grids only (staggered and hexagonal refused); no partial light or light levels; the fog image is one pixel per cell, drawn by the caller. Time not measured. | For light levels use `@margoengine/voxel/light-rgb` or a lighting pass; for hex fog test cells with `@margoengine/tilemap/hex` lines. |
| Pixel-art scaling (`@margoengine/pixel/scale`, 2026-11-08) | One pass a canvas view (or one into `target`), 4 texel reads a pixel for `'sharp-bilinear'` and up to 20 for `'edge'`; the picture covers whole screen pixels. | Covering each screen pixel by its share of each texel keeps art pixels flat and even at any size. | By method: two texels a side are mixed, so below 1 times the picture is not averaged over all it covers; `'edge'` below 2 times draws as `'sharp-bilinear'`; colours mix as stored (sRGB values), not in linear light; texels past the edge repeat the edge. | CRT look (`@margoengine/pixel/crt`, 2026-11-08) | One pass a canvas view (or one into `target`), 9 texel reads a pixel. | Working from the art's own rows keeps one scanline per art pixel at any screen size. | By method: a stylised look, not a model of a real tube (no beam spread with brightness, no persistence, no interlace, no colour bleed); one grille pattern (three columns); the art row under each pixel is taken whole, not mixed with the next; colours as stored, not in linear light. | Model outlines (`@margoengine/toon/models`, 2026-11-08) | One render pass a view for every outlined primitive, one hull draw a primitive and its instances (two pipelines: plain and mirrored nodes). | The hull reuses the vertices the model already has on the GPU, deformed ones included, so it costs one more vertex pass of the outlined triangles. | By method: an inverted hull, so the line follows vertex normals: hard-edged meshes with split normals show gaps at their creases; a constant world-unit width, thinner with distance; no line on point and line primitives; GPU-culled draws still draw their hull; one width and colour for every model. | Palette cycling and ramps (`@margoengine/pixel/palette`, 2026-11-08) | `cyclePalette` and `mixPalettes` run on the CPU per call; `setSwap` writes one 256 x 1 row at most each frame. | Rotating the drawn colours animates water and fire without repainting a pixel, and the matching stays. | By method: cycles rotate the colours drawn, not the matching (a pixel keeps its index); one rate per run, no ping-pong or easing; mixing is linear in Oklab between two palettes. | Hatching and halftone (`@margoengine/toon/hatch`, 2026-11-08) | Core meshes only, one shader patch: up to 4 stroke layers or one dot a pixel, in the mesh's own fragment pass. | A screen-space pattern needs no textures or UVs and keeps the same stroke width at any distance. | By method: the pattern is fixed to the screen, so it slides over a moving surface (no texture-space strokes); tone is Lambert n.l of the sun only (clustered lights and shadows are not inked); hatching steps by whole layers; the paper takes the full lit colour without the 1/pi of Lambert, as `ToonShading` does. | Text atlas eviction (`@margoengine/text`, 2026-11-08) | `TextRenderer.evictUnused()` and `GlyphAtlas.evict()` free texture array pages whose glyphs are no longer in any active visible `Text` block (LIM-572). | Per-glyph animation (`@margoengine/text/animate`, 2026-11-08) | `AnimatedText` drives position, scale, rotation, color and opacity per glyph quad over time (LIM-577). | Typewriter reveals and wave/bounce/color procedural motion while keeping global typography and line wrapping. | By method: each non-whitespace glyph is an individual `Text` block sharing the parent font and renderer, with individual model matrices and uniform colors; whitespace glyphs advance layout without GPU quads. | Extruded 3D text (`@margoengine/text/extrude`, 2026-11-08) | Enforced: nonzero fill, complete cap triangulation or a coded error; steps/curveSegments integers 1..256, bevelSegments 0..64; TrueType depth 32, 4,096 components and 200,000 raw points per glyph; Type 2 depth 10, 48 operands, 96 stems and 100,000 executed tokens; 16,384 flattened contour vertices per glyph and a conservative 1,000,000-vertex mesh budget per block.
